title: A pcheey whole selects a following value complement rather than naming a substance
summary: Use the exact pcheey X daiin recurrence to distinguish a constructional complement selector from a concrete material noun, generic H1 list field, or result marker.

design.mechanism: The complete pcheey whole marks or selects a following value/complement field in a dry-preparation/Form-II construction; it does not itself name the substance.
design.unit: Complete pcheey occurrences with independently coded following-field type, X-daiin complement relation, preparation/form context, and concrete substance status.
design.contrast: pcheey X daiin and matched pcheey lines without the complement against other H1 whole forms matched for paragraph-start position, moist/dry predecessor, and line ecology; substance-head and result-marker rivals are scored separately.
design.prediction: A complement-selector reading predicts a reproducible pcheey-to-following-value-field relation across distinct X fillers, including qoty and dal, while substance identity remains open. A substance-head model predicts material attachment; a result model predicts post-action/result context; a generic H1 field predicts no pcheey-specific complement enrichment.
design.falsifier: If independently bound held cases show no pcheey-specific following-field relation after position and predecessor controls, or if pcheey is consistently the independently identified substance head/result rather than a selector, this narrow selector hypothesis fails. The existing two-of-three recurrence is a motivation, not a semantic pass.
design.scope: GDT763's cached reader-exact pcheey frames only; independent field and substance endpoints are availability_unknown.
design.related: Related to GDT763, GDT764, GDT769, GDT775 and IDEA000010. It is a narrower constructional selector proposal, not a claim that pcheey is a source/reference pronoun, modality marker, amount unit, or named substance; the existing reports are predecessors and do not establish this binding.
design.countermodel: A generic H1 record field can happen to precede daiin in a small sample, while analyst renderer conventions or predecessor state create the apparent complement relation; a substance head can also take a value phrase without being a selector.

source_evidence.quote:
The best current `pcheey` reading is now narrower and more useful:

> **bound dry-preparation/Form-II record-content field with a following-value
> affinity; substance identity open**

It is not merely a generic list marker. Two of its three occurrences form the
reader-exact sequence `pcheey X daiin`, and all three lead into a recognizable
working content, quality, or amount neighborhood. At the same time, the right
fields are ordinary enough for H1 record ecology that they do not prove a
named ingredient. The local source reading “from/with dry material, Form II”
survives as a concrete C1 rival. The post-moist residue/result reading becomes
the weakest rival.
